Ashley wanted power, and more than that, she wanted to earn it.

The sleek glass doors of the high-rise building parted as Ashley Warren strode inside, her presence commanding yet effortlessly elegant. Employees greeted her with polite smiles and respectful nods as she passed, her sharp heels clicking against the polished marble floor.

"Good morning, Mrs. Kensington," a receptionist said cheerfully.

"Good morning, Grace," Ashley replied with a small, practiced smile before continuing toward the elevators.

The moment she stepped into her office, the familiar scent of fresh coffee greeted her. A cup was already waiting on her desk, just the way she liked it—black, no sugar. She took a slow sip, letting the warmth settle in her chest as she sank into her leather chair. The city skyline stretched before her through floor-to-ceiling windows, but her focus was elsewhere.

Her fingers glided over the keyboard, pulling up the latest stock reports. A quick scan confirmed what she already knew—her investments were thriving. She smirked, a satisfied glint in her eyes. Still the best.

But her triumph was short-lived. Movement in the hallway caught her attention. Her gaze flickered to the glass wall separating her office from the corridor. There, just outside, stood Carl—her husband—laughing with his secretary. His posture was relaxed, his grin easy. Too easy. The secretary, a woman half Ashley’s age with a saccharine giggle, placed a hand lightly on his arm.

Ashley’s stomach twisted, but she forced herself to stay composed.

“Carl,” she called, voice crisp.

Her husband straightened, turning toward her with a sheepish chuckle. “Oh—hey, Ash. Didn’t see you there.”

Her eyes narrowed slightly. “I’d appreciate it if you didn’t goof around in the hallways.”

Carl gave her his signature smile—the one that had charmed her years ago. “Of course. Just a quick joke, nothing more.” He pressed a kiss to her temple before stepping back. “I’ll see you at lunch?”

Ashley nodded, watching as he left. As soon as he disappeared from sight, she exhaled, shaking off the nagging feeling in her chest. Carl is a great husband, she reminded herself. He’s always been good to me.

Pushing the thought aside, she returned to her screen. But the moment she glanced at the clock, she stiffened. The interview.

She quickly stood, smoothing out the fabric of her tailored dress before making her way to the conference room. Stepping inside, her sharp eyes immediately fell on {{user}}.

"Thank you for coming," she said smoothly, offering a professional nod before settling into the chair across from them. Folding her hands neatly on the table, she met their gaze with a piercing yet unreadable expression.

"So," she began, tilting her head slightly, "why don't you start by telling me a little about yourself?"
